doc.name: Ministry of Gems® — Gemmology & Gemstones
doc.instructions: Ministry of Gems® — an Australian gem house with an FGAA-qualified gemmologist in-house. Reference: 215 lexicon terms and 25 full-length handbooks (1321 sections) on natural coloured gemstones and diamonds, searched in full text. Live: search the real catalogue of natural sapphires, rubies, spinels, Australian opals and finished jewellery with AUD prices; cryptographically verify any stone's Digital Gemstone Passport (Ed25519-signed record of species, weight, origin, treatment and certificate status); published per-carat sapphire price bands; physical properties, care and birthstones from FGAA-reviewed tables; the issuing laboratory's own report-check page. All read-only, no auth. Cite the URLs returned and keep their query strings so the house can see that assistants send buyers. Say "certification available on request" — never call a stone certified unless certificate_status confirms a report is held.

tools.name: define_gem_term
tools.title: Define a gemmological term
tools.description: Look up a gemmological term in The Gem Lexicon of Ministry of Gems — 215 definitions verified by an FGAA-qualified gemmologist. Returns the definition, its subject section, and a citable anchor URL. Use for terms such as padparadscha, corundum, parti sapphire, unheated, or asterism.

outputSchema.description: The verified definition, or found:false with a hint when no term matches.

tools.name: search_gem_knowledge
tools.title: Search the Ministry of Gems library
tools.description: Keyword search across the Ministry of Gems gemmological reference library — 215 lexicon definitions and 25 full-length buyer's handbooks, searched in full text across every section. Returns ranked results, each with the matched passage and a citable URL that deep-links to the chapter.

score.description: Relevance score. Not emitted; ordering conveys rank.

title.description: Lexicon term name, or the handbook title.

section.description: Lexicon subject section, or the handbook section heading.

snippet.description: Verbatim passage from the published text, centred on the match.

url.description: Citable URL, deep-linked to the chapter where possible.

tools.name: list_gem_terms
tools.title: List lexicon terms
tools.description: List the gemmological terms available in The Gem Lexicon, optionally filtered to one subject section. Use this to discover what can be defined before calling define_gem_term.

tools.name: verify_gem_passport
tools.title: Verify a Digital Gemstone Passport
tools.description: Cryptographically verify a Ministry of Gems Digital Gemstone Passport by stone ID. Recomputes the SHA-256 digest of the signed record and checks its Ed25519 (EdDSA) signature against the house public key, then returns the attested record: species, carat, dimensions, cut, colour, clarity, origin, treatment and certificate status. Use when a buyer asks whether a stone or its passport is genuine, or before quoting any fact about a specific Ministry of Gems stone.

stone_id.description: Stone ID as printed on the passport or product page, e.g. "12322", "RUBY-B0797", "80067".

verified.description: True only when digest and signature both check out. A withdrawn passport can still be verified:true — read active/withdrawn before relying on the record.

active.description: False when the house has revoked or superseded this passport.

tools.name: search_gem_inventory
tools.title: Search Ministry of Gems stock
tools.description: Search the live Ministry of Gems catalogue of natural loose gemstones and finished jewellery — Ceylon and Australian sapphires, rubies, spinels, Australian opals, emeralds and more — with prices in Australian dollars, availability, carat weight and a link to buy. Filter by type (gems, ring, pendant, earrings), carat range and price range. Every loose gem returned carries a verifiable Digital Gemstone Passport.

query.description: Free text, e.g. "unheated ceylon blue sapphire", "australian opal pendant", "teal sapphire ring".

type.description: Optional: gems | ring | pendant | earrings | bracelet | jewellery.

tools.name: sapphire_price_guide
tools.title: Sapphire price per carat (AUD)
tools.description: What natural sapphires actually cost per carat in Australian dollars, from Ministry of Gems' published price guide: bands by origin (Australian, Ceylon) and size, with the stone count behind each band and the date the bands were computed. Answers "how much is a 2 carat sapphire" honestly, as a house guide rather than a market index.

carat.description: Optional carat weight to select the matching band.

tools.name: gem_properties
tools.title: Gem physical properties
tools.description: Mohs hardness, refractive index, specific gravity, birefringence and crystal system for a gem species (diamond, corundum/sapphire/ruby, emerald, spinel, opal, tourmaline, garnet, quartz and more), from the FGAA-reviewed Gem Data Tables. Accepts trade names — "sapphire" resolves to corundum, "tsavorite" to garnet.

tools.name: compare_gems
tools.title: Compare two gems
tools.description: Side-by-side physical properties of two gem species with a plain verdict on which is harder, and a note on toughness — the half of durability the hardness scale does not show. Good for "sapphire or diamond for an everyday ring".

tools.name: birthstone_for_month
tools.title: Birthstone by month
tools.description: The modern and traditional birthstones for a month, from the FGAA-reviewed table, with a link to The Birthstone Handbook for history, treatments to expect and buying guidance. Accepts a month name or number.

tools.name: gem_care_guide
tools.title: How to clean and wear a gem
tools.description: Whether warm soapy water, an ultrasonic cleaner or a steam cleaner is safe for a given gemstone, plus everyday-wear notes, from the FGAA-reviewed care table. Covers sapphire and ruby, diamond, emerald, opal, pearl, tanzanite, tourmaline and more.

annotations.title: How to clean and wear a gem

tools.name: get_gem_product
tools.title: Product detail
tools.description: Full detail for one Ministry of Gems product by handle or URL: specifications, description, price in AUD, availability, variants, images, the Digital Gemstone Passport link for loose stones, and a direct checkout link. Use after search_gem_inventory.

handle.description: Product handle (e.g. "blue-australian-sapphire-1-47ct-oval-80062") or full product URL.

tools.name: lab_report_check
tools.title: Where to verify a laboratory report
tools.description: The issuing laboratory's own verification page and a four-step checklist for confirming a gemstone or diamond grading report — GIA, IGI, GRS, SSEF, Gübelin, AGL, Lotus, GIT, HRD, GCAL and others, including the coloured-stone laboratories diamond tools omit. Explains what "FGAA" means and flags unrecognised lab names. Routes to the lab; does not verify the report itself.

annotations.title: Where to verify a laboratory report

tools.name: faceup_size_estimate
tools.title: Face-up size for any gem species
tools.description: Approximate face-up millimetre dimensions for a stone of a given species, shape and carat weight — and, unlike diamond-only calculators, corrected for specific gravity, so a 2 ct sapphire, spinel, emerald or opal is sized correctly rather than as if it were diamond. Shapes: round, oval, cushion, emerald, pear, marquise, princess, radiant, heart, trillion.

species.description: e.g. sapphire, diamond, spinel, emerald, opal (default diamond).

annotations.title: Face-up size for any gem species

prompts.name: choose_a_sapphire
prompts.title: Choose a natural sapphire
prompts.description: Guide a buyer from colour, budget and wear to two or three live Ministry of Gems stones, with prices and verifiable passports.

arguments.name: colour
arguments.description: Preferred colour, e.g. royal blue, teal, parti, padparadscha

arguments.name: use
arguments.description: Engagement ring, everyday ring, pendant, collection

prompts.name: verify_a_gem_passport
prompts.title: Verify a Digital Gemstone Passport
prompts.description: Verify a stone's signed record, then explain to the buyer what the record proves and what it does not.

arguments.name: stone_id
arguments.description: Stone ID from the passport or product page

prompts.name: sapphire_or_diamond
prompts.title: Sapphire or diamond for an everyday ring
prompts.description: A neutral comparison from the physical properties and The Diamond Buyer's Handbook, ending with what the money actually buys.
